test.name: An autonomous run is a job even when the question looks bounded
test.description: Guards the e2e corpus against the 'Bounded request or job' section. Every e2e run enters as `/research --autonomous {researcher_question}` (eval/harness/e2e/orchestrator.py), so every run reads that section -- and 63 of the 136 committed e2e fixtures ask a question whose SHAPE is on the bounded list: 'Did X and Y have a son named Z', 'Who were the siblings of X', 'When and where did X die'. Without the `--autonomous` carve-out the router would deliver one answer and stop on those, instead of running the job the benchmark grades, and the e2e stop checker (e2e/stop_checker.py) has no `delivered` arm to even recognise the exit. The completeness sub-shape is the sharpest case because it was added to the bounded list by this same branch. GRADING: deterministic, via routes-to:question-selection -- the project has an objective and zero questions, so a job routes there first, and a bounded reading would stop instead.

judge_context: This is a ROUTING test. The hand-off is asserted deterministically; do not grade routing.

The question's shape is on the skill's own bounded list (whether a person's children are complete), but it arrives with `--autonomous`, which means drive it to completion. The correct behaviour is to run it as a JOB.
Do not penalise the reply for not naming a single deliverable, and do not reward it for stopping early. Stopping early is the failure this test exists to catch.
